why: Measure the PIE interlock behaviour on silicon, so that (a) the TRM-derived model in data/pie_pipeline.json
can be checked against the chip, and (b) the three instructions Table 1.7-2 omits (LD.QR, ST.QR, MV.QR,
p301-303) get a measured staging instead of no information at all.
Anchors are cases where the TRM states the stages: if they do not reproduce, the measurement method is
wrong and no result from this run may be used.

register_notes.qr: QR registers are q0-q7 in the assembler; the TRM's role names (qx, qy, qa, qz, qm, qu, qv, qs, qs0, qs1) are NOT accepted by this binutils, so each role is mapped to a concrete q number here and the mapping is what makes a case dependent or independent.
register_notes.as: The TRM's 'as' is the address operand slot of a PIE memory instruction: whatever AR is passed there.
register_notes.filler: add a14, a13, a12 is a native 1-cycle instruction, independent of every PIE register, used as issue-distance filler. It cancels between the dependent and independent variants of a case.

expect.why: TRM Table 1.7-2: EE.LD.ACCX.IP defs ACCX at 2 (M), EE.ST.ACCX.IP uses ACCX at 1 (E)
TRM Table 1.7-2: EE.VRELU.S16 defs qs at 2 (M), EE.MOV.S16.QACC uses qs at 1 (E)
TRM Table 1.7-2: EE.ANDQ defs qa at 1 (E); reading it in E needs no delay
calibration against the base ISA: a native load consumed by the next instruction costs 1 cycle (forwarding), which is what the harness must be able to resolve
calibration: back-to-back native ALU with a dependency costs nothing

cases.question: At which stage does LD.QR (p301, absent from Table 1.7-2) make qu available?
At which stage does MV.QR (p303) make qu available?
At which stage does ST.QR (p302) read qs? (producer is LD.QR, whose stage the case above measures)
Does LD.QR read its address operand (as) early enough that an instruction writing the AR costs nothing?
Cost of feeding a freshly loaded QR register into a vector op (the pattern real kernels use)
